topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture of the series and outlines the core learning outcomes on cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how successive genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion in pre-neoplastic tissues.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate whether tumors arise from tissue stem cells or committed progenitors, reviewing evidence for hierarchical cancer stem cell models across leukemias and colorectal cancers.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion and stromal dependency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stromal interactions are required to permit malignant outgrowth and tumor maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental technologies for studying tumor microenvironments and heterogeneity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to map cellular interactions and mutational histories in tumor tissues.

topics.label: Integrative multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesises the combined contributions of mutational burden, cell of origin, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental factors into a unified evolutionary model of malignancy.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming topic of cancer therapy.
